analysis_inventory.location: Per-entry external inventory maintained in an external audit workspace outside the canonical tree; one row per evaluated entry with decision and provenance.

sources.title: Goose
sources.decision_summary: Agent runtime with recipes, MCP extensions and extension lifecycle. Reference for extension lifecycle, load-time checks and reproducible scenarios; shell/edit/MCP effects and runtime-specific recipe assumptions are not portable to this framework.

sources.title: Agent Skills
sources.decision_summary: Engineering quality workflows: planning, context engineering, review, security, TDD, observability. 20 base candidates and 5 adaptations planned; all converted under framework contracts with behavior tests. npx installer and branch drift excluded; pinned-revision acquisition only.

sources.title: Anthropic alignment and adversarial evaluation research
sources.decision_summary: Design inspiration for adversarial/holdout evaluation only. Anti-self-approval and independent-review guarantees are enforced by acceptance.py and Host, not derived from any model vendor's practices; no constitutional corpus is copied or cited as authority.

sources.title: Anthropic prompts and tool-use cookbooks
sources.decision_summary: Reference for structured-output formatting (schema-validated JSON, model/version/prompt recording). Not a catalog source: names like semantic-diff-analyzer are rejected as unobservable; any structured-output need is met by neutral framework capabilities.

sources.title: Anthropic Cybersecurity Skills (community)
sources.decision_summary: 818 cybersecurity skills: 564 offensive/credential/malware/evasion procedures REJECTED outright; 254 defensive/compliance/forensics procedures kept reference-only. Never part of the default catalog; any future defensive adaptation requires written authorization, explicit scope and isolated execution.

sources.title: Anthropic Skills
sources.license: Per-skill LICENSE.txt terms; repository-level license not declared; some document skills are source-available, not open source
sources.decision_summary: Progressive disclosure, skill authoring and complex-skill structure patterns. 14 catalog candidates and 6 adaptations planned via contract conversion only; document-generation skills (docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx) are not copied due to source-available terms. Marketplace/npx install flows excluded.
sources.notes: License is heterogeneous: every conversion must record per-skill license evidence before contract work.

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Framework and Prescriptive Guidance
sources.decision_summary: aws-iam-policy-static-review is the first candidate if AWS evidence appears: static policy analysis, wildcard actions flagged, no credentials use, declared-vs-effective permissions distinguished. Cold-start optimization rejected until benchmarks are authorized.
sources.notes: Pin refers to the observed awsdocs/iam-user-guide snapshot; vendor terms remain per-page (proprietary).

sources.title: Clean Architecture
sources.decision_summary: Non-normative design bibliography. Creator/Host/generated-artifact boundaries predate and justify themselves; generated skills never depend on the Host as a runtime library. No catalog or base entry derives from this source.

sources.title: FastAPI framework and documentation
sources.decision_summary: Domain reference for OpenAPI contract checking. The catalog candidate fastapi-openapi-contract-check derives its activation signals and procedure from this ecosystem; activation only with FastAPI evidence in a project. Static, read-only checks; no real-service calls, no security inference from schema.

sources.title: Awesome Copilot
sources.decision_summary: 1021 community entries (435 skills, 226 agents, 194 instructions, 100 plugins, workflows/hooks). 159 catalog candidates and 142 adaptations identified per entry; community quality varies so every conversion needs per-entry provenance and acceptance. Onboarding/context-index patterns are the strongest transfer targets.

sources.title: gh-aw agentic workflows
sources.decision_summary: Agentic workflows compiled to GitHub Actions with read-only agents and safe-outputs. Primary value is Host-side pattern transfer (agent proposes, validated job applies; minimal permissions; analysis/mutation separation). 44 catalog candidates planned; GitHub Actions dependencies excluded from the framework runtime.

sources.title: Google SRE books and error budgets
sources.license: Free-to-read online; copyright Google, no text reuse
sources.decision_summary: Durable attempt/cost/time budgets with fail-closed exhaustion are implemented in budget.py and proportional-delivery; the methodology's SLO/SLA apparatus is not imported because the framework does not operate a measured service.

sources.title: Google engineering style guides
sources.decision_summary: Separate per-language candidates (typescript-strict-boundary-audit, go-concurrency-pattern-review) pending project evidence. Style compliance is never claimed as concurrency safety; compiler/test evidence and race-tooling authorization are prerequisites.

sources.title: HashiCorp Terraform and Vault guidance
sources.decision_summary: terraform-plan-drift-review candidate with supplied-plan scope; vault rotation verification requires execution evidence that static review cannot provide. Sensitive surface: no state/secret values in outputs, no apply/destroy, no Vault mutation.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 42001 AI management systems
sources.decision_summary: Postponed: no contractual requirement exists. Append-only decisions/metrics already cover operational traceability but do not assert AIMS conformity. If a requirement appears, build a dedicated compliance profile; never copy normative text into the tree.

sources.title: The Power of 10 Rules for safety-critical code
sources.license: Copyrighted article; citation only, no text redistribution
sources.decision_summary: Inspiration for explicit limits, return-value checks and rejection of unknown structure already enforced in host_validator, budgets and negative regressions. No skill is created; C-specific rules (fixed buffers, static analysis) do not transfer to this orchestrator context.

sources.title: JavaScript Mastery Skills
sources.decision_summary: Nine production phases (scope, audit, architect, develop, check, test, document, debug, sync) already adapted by architecture 3.0 as pattern source (commit 43b69e4 referenced in architecture). Remaining work: narrow contract conversion of the 9 skills; no runtime adoption, no npx, Host keeps all authority.

sources.title: Scientific Agent Skills
sources.license: MIT (repository); per-skill licenses heterogeneous incl. proprietary and CC BY-NC-SA
sources.decision_summary: 166 scientific skills. 17 narrow research-procedure adaptations planned (analysis, literature, statistics, peer review); 128 remain reference-only; 21 evidence-gated (cloud/lab integrations, clinical decision content). Per-skill license evidence is mandatory before any conversion.

sources.title: Last 30 Days research skill
sources.decision_summary: Single multi-source research skill with broad network providers, credential handling, first-run CLI auto-install and many helper scripts. Evidence-gated: requires project need, explicit authorization, allowlisted domains, read-only research and no auto-install before any adaptation is even considered.

sources.title: Marketing Skills
sources.decision_summary: 50 marketing/SEO/CRO skills. Reference only: commercial integrations, MCP/CLI dependencies and client-data surfaces make default incorporation inappropriate. Individual textual skills may be revisited only for a marketing project with explicit need.

sources.title: MDN Web Docs
sources.license: Site content and code samples under separate terms
sources.decision_summary: Reference for web-platform checks feeding http-security-headers-verifier candidates. Attribution and per-artifact terms must be fixed before reuse; browser/deployment context is required to judge CSP/CORS/SameSite claims.
sources.notes: Pin refers to the observed mdn/content repository snapshot; site terms remain per-artifact (mixed).

sources.title: Cloud Adoption Framework and Azure Architecture Center
sources.license: Copyrighted vendor documentation, free to read
sources.decision_summary: Outbox invariant checking is the only concrete candidate (messaging-outbox-verifier); distributed-resilience-audit rejected as too broad. Activated only by Azure/event-driven evidence; no service invocation or message publishing.

sources.title: MCP reference servers
sources.license: MIT to Apache-2.0 transition; verify per component and commit
sources.decision_summary: 7 reference MCP servers (fetch, git, time, memory, filesystem, sequentialthinking, everything). Technical reference for adapters and tool schemas only; declared educational by upstream. Never auto-connected; any future use needs sandboxing, roots, allowlists and its own tests.

sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.decision_summary: Risk classification and decision-record vocabulary only; never an automatic acceptance engine. Complementary to SSDF entry; pin edition before derived controls cite it.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF)
sources.decision_summary: Provenance matrix and evidence-custody practices inform workflow-evidence-management, decisions and receipts. Two distinct sources (SSDF and AI RMF) are registered separately. No compliance claims: framework controls do not assert NIST conformance. Pin edition and artifact digest before any derived control cites it.

sources.title: Superpowers
sources.decision_summary: Process skills: TDD, systematic debugging, writing/executing plans, code review, verification before completion. 9 base candidates and 5 adaptations planned. Git/worktree, harness and auto-discovery assumptions are excluded; verification gates become Host-enforced controls, not agent promises.

sources.title: OpenAI Skills (deprecated)
sources.license: No license file in pinned checkout; upstream deprecated in favor of openai/plugins
sources.decision_summary: Historical reference for skill-format evolution only. Unresolved license and deprecated upstream block any conversion; do not follow its conventions as current guidance.

sources.title: OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard
sources.decision_summary: Surface-gated preflight inspiration only: unpinned action references, symlink detection, dependency/script inventory. No universal Scorecard requirement; local projects without CI are evaluated differently, and no remote tooling is downloaded during bootstrap or accept.

sources.title: Oracle Architecture Center and Database 23ai documentation
sources.decision_summary: Candidate patterns (oracle-schema-migration-static-check, plsql static performance review) exist only when a project shows unambiguous Oracle evidence. No DSN connections, DDL/DML or EXPLAIN execution; static analysis of supplied artifacts only; version pinning required.

sources.title: OWASP GenAI/LLM Top 10
sources.decision_summary: Untrusted-content handling, secret detection and payload limits live in onboarding, inference channel and Host controls. The exact OWASP project/version must be disambiguated and pinned before any derived control cites it; risk lists never substitute for executed controls.

sources.title: Planning with Files
sources.decision_summary: Durable checkpoint/recovery concept for long tasks. The core planning skill is planned for reimplementation writing checkpoints outside the canonical tree with explicit ownership; the 17 auxiliary entries and the hooks (UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart/PreCompact/Stop with Write/Edit/Bash) are reference-only and rejected as-is.

sources.title: Pydantic validation library and documentation
sources.decision_summary: Model-layer domain reference for contract checking: typed request/response models underlie the OpenAPI surface. Cited as secondary source by fastapi-openapi-contract-check; Pydantic v1/v2 material differences require version pinning before any derived check.

sources.title: RHEL and CNCF security hardening guidance
sources.decision_summary: Candidates must split by layer: kubernetes-container-securitycontext-check (manifest) and oci-image-security-static-review (image). Runtime policy (seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux/admission) is never inferred from a Dockerfile; no builds or deployments.

sources.title: Rust guidelines and RustSec advisory database
sources.license: MIT/Apache-2.0; advisory DB under its own terms
sources.decision_summary: rust-unsafe-boundary-audit and rustsec-lockfile-advisory-check candidates pending a Rust project. Advisory DB must be snapshot-pinned; affected-version vs exploitability distinguished; build.rs never executed without isolation.

sources.title: Agentic Awesome Skills
sources.license: MIT (project code) plus LICENSE-CONTENT third-party material
sources.decision_summary: 6682 entries (2125 canonical skills, 4557 mirrors/bundles). Reference for evaluation, fault-injection and skill-review patterns. Whole-catalog import rejected: heterogeneous provenance, scripts/network/credentials, and names like 'security'/'acceptance' are not enforcement. Per-entry review required for anything specific.

sources.title: SQLite testing and fault-tolerance architecture
sources.license: Code public domain; documentation/site under separate terms
sources.decision_summary: Crash testing, byte-strict rollback and idempotency patterns are implemented as core transaction/recovery regressions (transaction.py, publisher, host_controller), not as a skill. No power-loss durability claim is made without dedicated evidence.

sources.title: Stitch Skills
sources.decision_summary: UI/Stitch-specific workflows. 9 adaptations planned but only activable when a project presents unambiguous Stitch/UI evidence and explicit authorization for remote MCP; remote endpoint, credential flows and asset-fetch scripts are excluded from conversion.

sources.title: Stripe API idempotency and API design patterns
sources.license: Copyrighted product documentation; no text/code reuse
sources.decision_summary: Generic pattern adopted in Host semantics: stable request identity per logical operation, reconcile-before-retry, prepared/published/acknowledged states, no blind resend after uncertain effects. Implemented in bootstrap/publisher/transaction regressions without copying vendor material.

sources.title: Vercel Agent Skills
sources.license: MIT recorded in inventory; per-skill terms not individually verified
sources.decision_summary: React/Vercel/React Native best-practice skills. 3 catalog candidates identified but blocked pending confirmation of per-skill terms; deploy/token skills are excluded outright. Promoted to CANDIDATE only after per-skill license verification at a pinned revision.

sources.title: Vercel Skills CLI
sources.decision_summary: Skill distribution/discovery CLI for many harnesses. Reference for catalog metadata and adapter design only; its npx/CLI installation model conflicts with the no-auto-acquisition policy and must not be adopted. Resolution of a skill never implies acceptance.

sources.title: Awesome Agent Skills
sources.license: Per-entry licenses; index itself has no uniform corpus license
sources.decision_summary: 1106 catalog links to third-party skills. Discovery index only: no local corpus, no uniform provenance. Each linked repository must be registered and audited individually before any use; the index is never cited as an authority for a skill's quality or license.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.license: W3C document license (open with attribution conditions)
sources.decision_summary: web-accessibility-wcag-audit candidate: requires declared target level (A/AA/AAA), separation of automated checks from manual keyboard/screen-reader review, and PARTIAL/UNVERIFIED when manual evidence is missing. Lighthouse-only conformity claims are prohibited.

sources.title: Agents plugin collection
sources.decision_summary: 485 entries (202 agents, 183 skills, 92 plugins, hooks/workflows). 101 catalog candidates identified; conversion requires narrowing to observable activation, de-duplication and capability filtering. Routing ambiguity and context overload risks documented; multi-harness claims are not treated as semantic equivalence.
